dedupe_keys.name: nlr evi x modelling suite electric vehicle charging infrastructure network planning site design and financial analysis tools

description: EVI-X is the National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) suite of electric vehicle charging infrastructure analysis tools, covering projects from national and state level down to site and facility operations. Contents: three groups of tools. Network planning tools (EVI-Pro and EVI-Pro Lite for light-duty charging needs, EVI-OnDemand for ride-hailing fleets, EVI-RoadTrip for highway corridors, EVI-DiST for distribution grid impacts) estimate the number, type and location of charging ports, power levels and grid impacts. Site design tools (EVI-InMotion for dynamic roadway charging, EVI-EnSitePy for site energy and layout, EDGES for behind-the-meter storage, EVI-Rental for rental car fleets, EVI-LOCATE for federal site assessment) inform station design. Financial tools such as EVI-FAST give station economics, levelized cost of charging and payback. Producer: NLR Transportation and Mobility Research. Coverage: United States. Format and access: a mix of NLR software, web tools (EVI-Pro Lite, EVI-LOCATE), open source GitHub code (EVI-DiST, EVI-OnDemand) and a registration download (EVI-FAST spreadsheet); contact EVI-X@nlr.gov. Licence: varies by tool and is not stated on the suite page. Caveats: several tools are used mainly in NLR-led custom analyses, not as public downloads. Simulation uses: sizing and siting charging networks, estimating charging loads for grid planning, and costing charging infrastructure.
